details.title: Digital Transformation Programme
details.courts_or_seat: City of Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

governing_law_source.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws and regulations in force in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. [...] the dispute shall be referred to the competent courts in the City of Riyadh, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, which shall have exclusive jurisdiction.

details.parties_quote: 1.1 Gulf Crown Hotels & Resorts Co., a closed joint stock company incorporated under the laws of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, holding Commercial Registration No. 1010584431, with its head office at King Fahd Road, Al Olaya District, P.O. Box 88214, Riyadh 11662, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (the "Company"); and 1.2 AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd, a private limited company incorporated under the laws of the Republic of India, bearing CIN U72900MH2019PTC321456, with its registered office at 4th Floor, Baner Business Bay, Pune 411045, Maharashtra, India (the "Service Provider").

payment_source.quote: The Company shall pay each undisputed invoice within sixty (60) days from the date of receipt of a valid invoice.

details.services_summary: Design, develop, test, deploy and support a revenue management and guest analytics platform for nine hotels in Saudi Arabia.

liability_cap.quote: Save in respect of liability arising from fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of Clause 7 (Confidentiality) or Clause 13 (Data Protection), each Party's aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the Contract Value.

delay_penalty.quote: Should the Service Provider fail to achieve any Milestone by its scheduled completion date, the Service Provider shall pay to the Company, by way of liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to one percent (1%) of the Contract Value for each week or part thereof of delay.

findings.title: Al Noor Hospitality Group: Data analytics, AI or revenue-management services
findings.why: The deal involves revenue management and guest analytics for hotels in Saudi Arabia, which directly conflicts with the non-compete scope covering hospitality businesses in Saudi Arabia.
findings.comparison: Do not take analytics, AI or revenue-management work for hotel groups in the GCC until about September 2029 without Al Noor's written consent.
findings.quote: the Supplier undertakes that neither it nor any of its Affiliates shall, during the Restricted Period, directly or indirectly, provide data analytics, artificial intelligence or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business in the GCC.
findings.exception: Clause 12.4 lets Al Noor waive it per engagement by written consent. Waiver letter of 10 Feb 2026 allows only the Seaside Hotels (Muscat) demand-forecasting SOW; not follow-on SOWs, other hotels or Affiliates.

findings.title: Unilateral IP Indemnity
findings.why: The indemnity is one-sided. AtliQ is solely responsible for IP infringement claims without a reciprocal indemnity from the client for client-provided materials.
findings.quote: The Service Provider shall indemnify the Company against all losses, claims and expenses arising from any claim by a third party that the Deliverables infringe the intellectual property rights of such third party.

findings.title: High Delay Penalty Calculation
findings.why: The penalty is based on the total Contract Value ($140,000) rather than the specific milestone fee, which could lead to disproportionate financial exposure.
findings.comparison: Past contracts typically use a percentage of the milestone fee, not the total contract value.
findings.quote: the Service Provider shall pay to the Company, by way of liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to one percent (1%) of the Contract Value for each week or part thereof of delay.

findings.title: Missing Client-Caused Delay Exclusion
findings.why: The clause fails to exclude delays caused by the client or scope changes, leaving AtliQ liable for delays outside its control.
findings.comparison: AtliQ principles require explicit exclusion of client-caused delays.
findings.quote: The Service Provider shall not be liable for delay to the extent such delay is caused by a Force Majeure Event as defined in Clause 15.

findings.title: Arabic text prevails in case of inconsistency
findings.why: If AtliQ does not have internal Arabic legal review, it risks being bound by terms in the Arabic version that differ from the English version.
findings.comparison: Unusual; most AtliQ contracts are English-only.
findings.quote: In the event of any inconsistency, the Arabic text shall prevail.

findings.title: Indian entity under non-Indian law (Kingdom of Saudi Arabia)
findings.why: Disputes would be fought under foreign law and courts.
findings.comparison: Principle: India for AtliQ Pvt Ltd. Past exceptions (Al Noor DIFC, Northwind English law) were deliberate.
findings.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws and regulations in force in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

findings.title: Payment in 60 days
findings.why: Long payment terms hurt cash flow.
findings.quote: The Company shall pay each undisputed invoice within sixty (60) days from the date of receipt of a valid invoice.

findings.title: Uncompensated transition assistance
findings.why: The clause does not explicitly state that transition services are billable, potentially requiring AtliQ to work for free.
findings.comparison: Standard contracts usually specify that transition services are provided at agreed rates.
findings.quote: shall provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of up to sixty (60) days.

findings.title: Termination for convenience payment limitation
findings.why: Limiting payment to 'accepted' work creates a risk that AtliQ is not paid for completed work if the client refuses acceptance.
findings.comparison: AtliQ prefers payment for all work performed, regardless of formal acceptance status.
findings.quote: the Company shall pay for all Services performed and accepted up to the date of termination.

findings.title: Data Residency Restriction
findings.why: This restricts AtliQ's ability to use its standard global cloud infrastructure or offshore development teams without client approval.
findings.comparison: This is a specific operational constraint not present in standard AtliQ contracts.
findings.quote: Guest Data shall be hosted within the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia unless the Company provides prior written approval for any transfer outside the Kingdom.

findings.title: Data residency requirement
findings.why: Restricts AtliQ's ability to use its standard global cloud infrastructure, potentially increasing operational costs.
findings.comparison: More restrictive than standard contracts which do not specify data location.

findings.title: Subcontracting requires prior written consent
findings.why: Limits AtliQ's operational flexibility to use subcontractors for specific tasks without client approval.
findings.comparison: Standard, but requires careful management of project delivery timelines.
findings.quote: The Service Provider shall not assign or subcontract any of its obligations without the prior written consent of the Company.
